title: Claim status transitions with an audit note
tagline: Implement the allowed status moves for a claim, then add an audit-note change request.
intro: Hi, thanks for making the time. I am the consultant developer on the claim intake team. Today we will work in the claim domain: a claim moves through OPEN, IN_REVIEW, and CLOSED, and I want a small pure Java helper that owns those transitions. Ask me anything before you start.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Which status transitions are allowed?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Requesting the same status is an idempotent no-op. OPEN may only move to IN_REVIEW. IN_REVIEW may move to OPEN or CLOSED. CLOSED is terminal, so it cannot move to a different status.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask which moves are legal before writing the switch or if-chain.

clarifyingQuestions.question: What should happen when a transition is not allowed?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Throw IllegalStateException, and include both the current and target status in the message so the caller can log a useful audit line. A null argument should throw NullPointerException.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask how invalid moves fail, and whether the error message must name the statuses.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is setting the same status again allowed?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Treat it as a no-op and return the same status. Do not throw, because retries from a client should be harmless.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask about idempotency and repeated requests.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Should this touch persistence, threads, or an audit log?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: No. For this round keep it a pure in-memory function. No repository, no threads, no logging. The change request will add a small audit object, but still without persistence.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask whether the helper is pure or whether it should persist or log anything.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Will there be a follow-up change?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: Yes. After the first round I will add a change request around audit metadata and reopening rules. Design the base so that extension is not painful.
clarifyingQuestions.coach: Ask whether a change request is coming and what kind of extension to expect.

clarifyingFallback: For this round, assume the helper is a pure in-memory Java utility. If a detail is not specified, choose the simplest rule, say the assumption out loud, and keep the change request in mind.
problemStatement:
### Context

You are working on the claim intake API. A claim has three statuses: OPEN, IN_REVIEW, and CLOSED.

### Your task

Implement ClaimStatusMachine with two static methods:

1. canTransition(current, target) returns true when the move is allowed.
2. transition(current, target) returns the target status when the move is allowed.

### Rules

- Requesting the same status is an allowed no-op.
- OPEN may move only to IN_REVIEW.
- IN_REVIEW may move to OPEN (reopened) or CLOSED.
- CLOSED is terminal and cannot move to a different status.
- Null arguments throw NullPointerException.
- An illegal move throws IllegalStateException whose message names both statuses.

### Visible examples

- OPEN to IN_REVIEW: allowed, returns IN_REVIEW.
- IN_REVIEW to OPEN: allowed, returns OPEN.
- OPEN to CLOSED: rejected with IllegalStateException.
- CLOSED to OPEN: rejected with IllegalStateException.
- OPEN to OPEN: allowed no-op.

### Notes

- Keep the class in the default package and in the starter file.
- The hidden tests call the static methods directly.

hiddenTests.name: same status is an allowed no-op
OPEN moves to IN_REVIEW
IN_REVIEW moves to CLOSED
IN_REVIEW can reopen to OPEN
CLOSED is terminal
OPEN cannot jump straight to CLOSED
illegal transition message names both statuses
null statuses are rejected

probes.text: Before you write the branches, tell me which transitions you are rejecting and why.
What should happen if the same status is requested twice? Is that a transition or a no-op?

fallbackProbe: Which part of the state machine is easiest to get wrong, and how would you prove it with a test?

phasePrompts.brief: Read the problem, then ask me the questions you would ask a real interviewer. When you are ready, tell me your plan and start the clock.
phasePrompts.implement: The implementation timer is running. Talk through your approach as you code, and tell me when you want to run the tests.
phasePrompts.test: Run the tests. Read the first failure carefully, say what you think caused it, then fix it.
phasePrompts.change: Here is the change request. Treat it as new scope from the interviewer, not as a rewrite of everything you have done.
phasePrompts.debrief: Time is up. Let us review what happened: the tests, the rubric, your questions, and the hints you used.

hints: Start by listing the legal pairs on paper. There are only three statuses, so a small if-chain or switch is enough.
Handle the same-status no-op before the terminal-status check. Then let OPEN only target IN_REVIEW and let IN_REVIEW target OPEN or CLOSED.
The illegal path should throw new IllegalStateException with a message built from both enum values. Reuse canTransition from transition so the rules live in one place.

changeRequest.prompt: Add audit metadata and a reopening rule.
changeRequest.statement:
### Change request

The claims team now needs an audit-friendly overload.

Add a record named Transition with three components: from, to, and note. Add an overload:

transition(current, target, note)

Requirements:

- Validate the move with the existing transition(current, target) rules.
- If the target is OPEN, the note is mandatory and must not be blank after trimming. Otherwise throw IllegalArgumentException.
- For any other target, a null note is allowed and becomes an empty string.
- Return the note trimmed, never null.
- Illegal moves must still throw IllegalStateException.

Keep the original two-argument method working exactly as before.

hiddenTests.name: reopening requires a non-blank note
reopen returns a Transition record with a trimmed note
closing accepts a blank or null note
an invalid move still throws even with a note
null target with a note is rejected

rubric.criterion: Base transition rules pass the hidden suite
rubric.strongAnswer: All base tests pass: same-status no-op, allowed moves, terminal CLOSED, and clear failures for illegal moves.

rubric.criterion: Audit-note change request passes the hidden suite
rubric.strongAnswer: The overload returns a trimmed Transition record, requires a note only for reopening, and preserves the base rules.
Asked about allowed moves, failure behaviour, idempotency, and scope before committing to an implementation.
Reached a correct design with no hints, or used one hint only after a genuine attempt.
Finished implementation, testing, and the change request inside the time budget without rushing the tests.
